First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot {7}^{4x+2} & <-{x}^{2}\cdot {7}^{4x+1} \\ {x}^{2}\cdot {7}^{4x+1}+x\cdot {7}^{4x+2} & <0 \\ {x}^{2}\cdot {7}^{4x+1}+7x\cdot {7}^{4x+1} & <0 \\ ({x}^{2}+7x)\cdot {7}^{4x+1} & <0 \\ x(x+7)\cdot {7}^{4x+1} & <0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by ${7}^{4x+1}$ and get

$$
x(x+7)<0.
$$

This represents an upwards parabola whose roots are at $x=-7$ and $x=0.$ The parabola is below the $x$-axis when $-7<x<0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013930/assets/b884ee15f864bcd02639085dc1465a82958ef0faeb9408e68b405c5906ea3a18.png)

Therefore, the solution is $-7<x<0.$
